literature.headline_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期基孔肯雅病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 2023 年,三个埃及伊蚊池检测出 CHIKV 阳性,系统发育分析证实东部/中部/南非 (ECSA) 谱系的循环与人类 暴发 相关序列密切相关。 [10.1016/j.actatropica.2026.108299]
指标病例于2025年8月6日确认,追溯检测首例症状出现时间为7月31日;原发病例未被识别。截至10月15日,报告69例病例(62例确诊,7例可能),平均年龄55岁;91.3%病例具有明确流行病学关联,主要集中在维罗纳省的两个市镇。 [10.1093/jtm/taag079]
这些区别很重要:未经调整的血清阳性率可能会夸大或掩盖 CHIKV 传播 的估计值,并且没有一个诊断平台可以解决每个病毒对的问题。我们认为,共流行环境中的 CHIKV 诊断 需要分层策略:急性期进行分子检测,随后进行抗原告知和多重 血清学,以及基于中和的确认(其中归因至关重要),并结合 监测 的交叉反应感知统计模型。 [10.30574/wjarr.2026.31.2.2014]

其中,16.5%的患者需要入院,中位住院时间为5天(IQR 3-6),其余患者在室外就诊。参与者的平均 (SD) 年龄为 45·3 (15·5) 岁,其中 60% 为女性。发烧(98%)和关节痛(97%)是主要症状。6% 的患者报告轻度疼痛,40% 的患者报告中度疼痛,54% 的患者报告重度疼痛,VAS 评分中位数为 8.0(IQR 7.0-9.0)。超过 70% 的参与者报告了行动受限、自我护理、功能障碍、疼痛或心理症状。EQ-5D 指数中位数为 0·78 (IQR 0·60-0·96)。 [10.1371/journal.pntd.0014599]
传播 对两种病毒的适宜性集中在南方夏季(11 月至 4 月),冬季值接近于零,低于指示性 传播 阈值(指数 P ≥ 0.5)。基孔肯雅热的适宜性始终高于登革热,在空间上更广泛且持续时间更长,所有地区均超过基孔肯雅热阈值(指数 P = 0.71),而登革热仍低于阈值(中位指数 P = 0.24)。 [10.64898/2026.08.23.26361159]

The index case was identified on 6 August 2025, with retrospective detection of the first case with symptom onset on 31 July; the primary case was not identified. [10.1093/jtm/taag079]

The most consistent associations were female sex (OR 2.08, 95% CI 1.77–2.46; I2=8.3%), comorbidity presence (1.99, 1.55–2.55; I2=0%), and high blood pressure (1.52, 1.13–2.04; I2=33.4%). [10.1093/jtm/taag078]

These distinctions matter: unadjusted seropositivity can inflate or obscure CHIKV transmission estimates, and no single diagnostic platform resolves the problem for every virus pair. [10.30574/wjarr.2026.31.2.2014]

Of all, 16.5% of patients required hospital admission, with a median length of stay of 5 days (IQR 3-6), and the rest of them consulted on an outdoor basis. The mean (SD) age of the participants was 45·3 (15·5) years, and 60% were female. Fever (98%) and arthralgia (97%) were the predominant symptoms. [10.1371/journal.pntd.0014599]

news.headline_zh: 法国本土基孔肯雅热病例上升,欧洲多国发布警报与防控建议。
news.lead_zh: 2026年8月,法国南部及多地报告25例本土感染基孔肯雅热病例,触发法国公共卫生机构发布年度警报并加强蚊媒控制;同期印度泰伦加纳邦病例下降、浦那启动每日灭蚊,巴西与德国联合研发的新型疫苗在小鼠实验中显示保护效果。
key_findings_zh: 法国2026年夏季已确认25例本土基孔肯雅热病例,输入病例110例,当局在吉伦特省与塔恩省实施灭蚊与户外活动限制 [news-6ee3f016677d47c5]。
法国于8月底再次发布南部地区基孔肯雅热警报,白纹伊蚊已在居民区定殖,5月至11月为高风险传播期 [news-0e493e16732f1e23]。
印度泰伦加纳邦2026年1至8月基孔肯雅热、登革热、疟疾等蚊媒疾病病例较去年同期下降,官方正加强流感样疾病监测 [news-7799583724e49381]。
印度浦那市政委员会下令每日开展灭蚊喷雾与雾化行动,旨在遏制登革热与基孔肯雅热传播 [news-bb8f7a65dc51c553]。
巴西与德国研究人员开发的新型基孔肯雅热疫苗在小鼠实验中单剂即可提供保护,并计划进入临床试验阶段 [news-948612872fea4e90]。
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 气候变化与白纹伊蚊扩散正推动基孔肯雅热在欧洲南部形成本土传播链;南亚多国仍面临季节性蚊媒疾病压力,但部分地区通过防控措施使疫情有所缓解,新型疫苗研究为未来防控提供新工具。
news.caveats_zh: 浦那病例上升与官方具体数字尚不明确,部分来源未提供详细风险等级数据;新型疫苗结果仅基于动物实验,尚未开展人体试验。
news.headline_en: France reports rising local chikungunya cases as Europe heightens alerts and India steps up mosquito control.
news.lead_en: In late August 2026, France confirmed 25 locally acquired chikungunya cases during summer, prompting renewed alerts across southern regions and intensified vector control. Meanwhile, India's Telangana state recorded declines in mosquito-borne diseases while Pune launched daily anti-mosquito drives, and a Brazil–Germany research team reported promising single-dose vaccine results in mice.
key_findings_en: France confirmed 25 locally acquired chikungunya cases in summer 2026, with 110 imported cases; insecticide spraying and temporary bans on outdoor sports were deployed in Gironde and Tarn [news-6ee3f016677d47c5].
France reissued a chikungunya alert for southern regions, citing established Aedes albopictus populations and a high-risk transmission window from May to November [news-0e493e16732f1e23].

India's Telangana state reported declines in dengue, malaria, chikungunya and other vector-borne diseases from January to August 2026 compared with last year, while monitoring for influenza-like illness [news-7799583724e49381].
Pune Municipal Corporation ordered daily anti-mosquito spraying and fogging drives and sought to expedite hiring of 265 contractual workers to curb dengue and chikungunya [news-bb8f7a65dc51c553].

A Brazil–Germany team reported a single-dose chikungunya vaccine candidate that protected mice from lethal infection and reduced joint inflammation, with clinical trials planned [news-948612872fea4e90].
news.trend_or_risk_en: Climate-driven expansion of Aedes albopictus is enabling persistent local chikungunya transmission in southern Europe, while South Asian cities continue to face seasonal vector-borne risks that are being addressed through intensified mosquito control and surveillance. Novel vaccine candidates may strengthen future response but remain in early-stage research.
news.caveats_en: Specific case numbers and risk levels for Pune's chikungunya uptick were not detailed in available reporting; the new vaccine findings are limited to mouse models and have not yet entered human trials.

A Brazil–Germany research team reported that a single dose of a new chikungunya vaccine candidate protected mice from lethal infection and reduced joint inflammation, paving the way for planned clinical trials.

papers.title: Predictors of chronic arthralgia after chikungunya virus infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Chikungunya is an expanding global health threat, with chronic arthralgia representing the main long-term driver of disability. Although many studies have assessed post-chikungunya outcomes, evidence remains fragmented and contradictory. We aimed to identify reproducible predictors of chronic arthralgia (≥3 months) after laboratory-confirmed chikungunya and to distinguish stable prognostic signals from context-dependent associations. Methods We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and BVS/LILACS from inception to Feb 6, 2026, without restrictions. Eligible studies compared participants with and without chronic arthralgia at follow-up and reported extractable baseline or acute-phase factors. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using QUIPS. Random-effects restricted maximum likelihood meta-analyses pooled odds ratios and mean differences, with subgroup analyses by follow-up window. PROSPERO: CRD420251169320. Results Of 1784 records, 29 studies were included, comprising 4108 participants: 1838 with chronic arthralgia and 2230 without. After harmonization, 22 predictors were meta-analyzed. The most consistent associations were female sex (OR 2.08, 95% CI 1.77–2.46; I2=8.3%), comorbidity presence (1.99, 1.55–2.55; I2=0%), and high blood pressure (1.52, 1.13–2.04; I2=33.4%). In contrast, several acute-phase manifestations and treatment-related markers showed less stable, timing-dependent, or study-sensitive associations. Overall risk of bias was high in most studies and moderate in the remainder. Conclusions Chronic post-chikungunya arthralgia was most reproducibly associated with readily identifiable baseline host factors, rather than with a uniform acute-severity phenotype. These findings suggest that risk stratification should not rely only on acute symptom burden, and that pre-existing vulnerability may define a clinically important high-risk group. Point-of-care identification of patients with these characteristics could support prioritization of follow-up and resource allocation during outbreaks, inform post-outbreak surveillance and guideline development, and may guide future burden-based vaccination strategies in endemic settings.

papers.title: Autochthonous chikungunya virus outbreak in Verona province, Italy, 2025.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), primarily transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, has increasingly caused autochthonous outbreaks in temperate regions, including Italy. In 2025, a local CHIKV outbreak occurred in Verona province, Veneto Region. We report the findings of integrated epidemiological, virological, and entomological investigations. Methods In 2025, a dedicated surveillance protocol was implemented to assess local transmission of arboviral infections in Verona province, enabling early detection of a local CHIKV circulation. Following notification of the index case, investigations were conducted in accordance with the national and regional arbovirus surveillance plans, including comprehensive epidemiological, virological, and entomological analyses. Results The index case was identified on 6 August 2025, with retrospective detection of the first case with symptom onset on 31 July; the primary case was not identified. As of 15 October, 69 cases were reported (62 confirmed, 7 probable), with a mean age of 55 years; 91.3% had identifiable epidemiological links, mainly clustered in two municipalities of the Verona province. Most cases (76.8%) occurred between mid-August and mid-September. The outbreak lasted approximately fifteen weeks, from the end of July to the mid of October. CHIKV-RNA was detectable in whole blood and, less frequently, urine only within the first five days after symptom onset, with higher viral loads in blood. CHIKV-specific IgM antibodies were detectable from days 4–5 and IgG from days 7–10. A total of 225 Aedes albopictus specimens were collected, all testing negative for CHIKV. Phylogenetic analysis revealed a highly homogeneous, monophyletic cluster within the East-Central-South African (ECSA) genotype, closely related to strains from the 2024–2025 Réunion outbreak. Conclusions This outbreak underscores the value of dedicated surveillance protocols for early detection of febrile/suspected arboviral cases, while also highlighting key vulnerabilities, namely, an undetected primary case and negative entomological findings, pointing to the need for lower testing thresholds and earlier, risk-based vector sampling.

papers.title_zh: 意大利维罗纳省2025年本土性基孔肯雅病毒 暴发暴发
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), primarily transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, has increasingly caused autochthonous outbreaks in temperate regions, including Italy. In 2025, a local CHIKV outbreak occurred in Verona province, Veneto Region. We report the findings of integrated epidemiological, virological, and entomological investigations. Methods In 2025, a dedicated surveillance protocol was implemented to assess local transmission of arboviral infections in Verona province, enabling early detection of a local CHIKV circulation. Following notification of the index case, investigations were conducted in accordance with the national and regional arbovirus surveillance plans, including comprehensive epidemiological, virological, and entomological analyses. Results The index case was identified on 6 August 2025, with retrospective detection of the first case with symptom onset on 31 July; the primary case was not identified. As of 15 October, 69 cases were reported (62 confirmed, 7 probable), with a mean age of 55 years; 91.3% had identifiable epidemiological links, mainly clustered in two municipalities of the Verona province. Most cases (76.8%) occurred between mid-August and mid-September. The outbreak lasted approximately fifteen weeks, from the end of July to the mid of October. CHIKV-RNA was detectable in whole blood and, less frequently, urine only within the first five days after symptom onset, with higher viral loads in blood. CHIKV-specific IgM antibodies were detectable from days 4–5 and IgG from days 7–10. A total of 225 Aedes albopictus specimens were collected, all testing negative for CHIKV. Phylogenetic analysis revealed a highly homogeneous, monophyletic cluster within the East-Central-South African (ECSA) genotype, closely related to strains from the 2024–2025 Réunion outbreak. Conclusions This outbreak underscores the value of dedicated surveillance protocols for early detection of febrile/suspected arboviral cases, while also highlighting key vulnerabilities, namely, an undetected primary case and negative entomological findings, pointing to the need for lower testing thresholds and earlier, risk-based vector sampling.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 主要由伊蚊传播,在包括意大利在内的温带地区越来越多地引起本土 暴发。2025年,威尼托大区维罗纳省发生了一场当地的CHIKV 暴发。我们报告综合流行病学、病毒学和昆虫学调查的结果。方法 2025 年,实施了专门的 监测 方案来评估维罗纳省当地 传播 虫媒病毒感染,从而能够及早发现当地 CHIKV 循环。通报指示病例后,根据国家和地区虫媒病毒监测计划进行了调查,包括全面的流行病学、病毒学和昆虫学分析。结果 2025年8月6日发现指示病例,7月31日回顾发现首例出现症状的病例;原发病例尚未确定。截至 10 月 15 日,报告了 69 例病例(62 例确诊,7 例疑似),平均年龄 55 岁;91.3% 有可识别的流行病学联系,主要集中在维罗纳省的两个市。大多数病例(76.8%)发生在八月中旬至九月中旬之间。暴发 持续了大约十五周,从七月底到十月中旬。仅在症状出现后的前五天内,全血和尿液中可检测到 CHIKV-RNA,血液中的病毒载量较高。在第 4-5 天可检测到 CHIKV 特异性 IgM 抗体,在第 7-10 天可检测到 IgG。共采集了 225 份白纹伊蚊样本,所有 CHIKV 检测均呈阴性。系统发育分析揭示了南非中东部(ECSA)基因型内存在高度同质的单系簇,与 2024-2025 年留尼汪 暴发 菌株密切相关。结论 本 暴发 强调了专用 监测 方案对于早期检测发热/疑似虫媒病毒病例的价值,同时也强调了关键漏洞,即未检测到的原发病例和阴性昆虫学发现,指出需要较低的检测阈值和更早、基于风险的 媒介 采样。

papers.title: Mosquito diversity and arbovirus detection in Paraguay: first evidence of dengue and chikungunya virus infection in field populations.
papers.abstract: Arboviruses are mosquito-borne viruses of major public health importance, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions. In Paraguay, dengue (DENV) and chikungunya (CHIKV) viruses are among the most epidemiologically relevant; however, studies integrating mosquito and arbovirus surveillance remain scarce. This study aimed to characterize mosquito assemblage composition across different ecological settings and investigate arbovirus circulation in field-collected mosquitoes. A total of 4,595 mosquitoes (609 pools) were collected between 2013 and 2024 from urban, rural, and Atlantic Forest environments in Paraguay. Twenty-six mosquito species were identified, with Culex quinquefasciatus (55.3%) as the most abundant, followed by Aedes (Ochlerotatus) scapularis (13.3%). Aedes aegypti (7.3%) was mainly associated with urban areas. Diversity analyses showed higher alpha diversity and greater gamma diversity in the Atlantic Forest and lower values in rural areas, whereas high beta diversity indicated substantial species turnover among locations. Molecular screening by real-time RT-PCR detected no evidence of West Nile, Saint Louis encephalitis, Venezuelan equine encephalitis, Mayaro, yellow fever, Zika, or Oropouche viruses. aegypti pools tested positive for DENV (n=3; 2021 and 2023) and CHIKV (n=3; 2023). Phylogenetic reconstruction confirmed the circulation of DENV-4 Genotype II (lineage B.1.1), DENV-2 Genotype II (F.1.1.2), and CHIKV East/Central/South African (ECSA) lineages in Paraguay, all closely related to human outbreak-associated sequences. These findings provide the first molecular evidence of arbovirus infection in field-collected mosquitoes in Paraguay and emphasize the importance of integrated entomological and viral surveillance.

papers.abstract_zh: 虫媒病毒是蚊媒病毒,对公共卫生具有重要意义,特别是在热带和亚热带地区。在巴拉圭,登革热 (DENV) 和基孔肯雅 (CHIKV) 病毒属于流行病学最相关的病毒;然而,整合蚊子和虫媒病毒 监测 的研究仍然很少。本研究旨在表征不同生态环境下的蚊子组合组成,并研究现场收集的蚊子中的虫媒病毒循环。2013 年至 2024 年间,从巴拉圭的城市、农村和大西洋森林环境中总共收集了 4,595 只蚊子(609 个池)。已鉴定出 26 种蚊子,其中致倦库蚊 (55.3%) 数量最多,其次是肩胛伊蚊 (Ochlerotatus) (13.3%)。埃及伊蚊(7.3%)主要与城市地区有关。多样性分析显示,大西洋森林的α多样性和伽玛多样性较高,而农村地区的值较低,而高的β多样性表明不同地点之间存在大量物种更替。通过实时 RT-PCR 进行的分子筛查未发现西尼罗河病毒、圣路易斯脑炎、委内瑞拉马脑炎、马亚罗病毒、黄热病、寨卡病毒或奥罗普切病毒的证据。埃及伊蚊池检测出 DENV(n=3;2021 年和 2023 年)和 CHIKV(n=3;2023 年)呈阳性。系统发育重建证实了DENV-4基因型II(谱系B.1.1)、DENV-2基因型II(F.1.1.2)和CHIKV东/中/南非(ECSA)谱系在巴拉圭的循环,所有这些谱系都与人类暴发相关序列密切相关。这些发现提供了巴拉圭现场采集的蚊子中虫媒病毒感染的第一个分子证据,并强调了综合昆虫学和病毒 监测 的重要性。

papers.title: Chikungunya Virus serological cross-reactivity in co-endemic settings: Mechanisms, Diagnostic implications, and epidemiological consequences
papers.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) causes an acute febrile illness with debilitating arthralgia, and serological assays remain central to its diagnosis and surveillance. However, antibody-based results are complicated by cross-reactivity in settings where multiple arboviruses co-circulate. This review distinguishes three related but distinct phenomena affecting CHIKV serology: biological cross-reactivity, arising from genuine antigenic overlap between related viruses; assay-associated non-target reactivity, in which a diagnostic platform generates a positive signal without an established biological relationship between the viruses; and diagnostic misclassification, the downstream epidemiological consequence of conflating the two. Applying this framework to five virus pairs, we find that CHIKV–O'nyong-nyong virus (ONNV), CHIKV–Mayaro virus (MAYV) and CHIKV–Ross River virus (RRV) relationships are supported by shared alphavirus antigenic architecture and, in several studies, by functional cross-neutralisation. By contrast, CHIKV reactivity reported in dengue virus (DENV)- and Zika virus (ZIKV)-associated sera lacks an established biological basis and is better classified as assay-associated non-target reactivity of unresolved mechanism. These distinctions matter: unadjusted seropositivity can inflate or obscure CHIKV transmission estimates, and no single diagnostic platform resolves the problem for every virus pair. We argue that CHIKV diagnosis in co-endemic settings requires a layered strategy: molecular detection during the acute phase, antigenically informed and multiplex serology thereafter, and neutralisation-based confirmation where attribution is critical, combined with cross-reactivity-aware statistical modelling for surveillance. Strengthening assay validation and confirmatory testing, particularly in African settings such as Nigeria where CHIKV, DENV and related alphaviruses circulate together, is essential for improving diagnostic accuracy and epidemiological inference.
papers.journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the mechanisms of serological cross-reactivity in Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in co-endemic settings, emphasizing the challenges it poses for diagnosis and surveillance. The study identifies three distinct phenomena affecting CHIKV serology: biological cross-reactivity, assay-associated non-target reactivity, and diagnostic misclassification. It highlights that cross-reactivity with O'nyong-nyong virus (ONNV), Mayaro virus (MAYV), and Ross River virus (RRV) is supported by shared antigenic architecture and functional cross-neutralisation, while cross-reactivity with dengue virus (DENV) and Zika virus (ZIKV) lacks a biological basis. The review underscores the need for a layered diagnostic approach, including molecular detection, antigenically informed serology, and neutralisation-based confirmation, along with cross-reactivity-aware statistical models. It also stresses the importance of improving assay validation and confirmatory testing in regions where multiple arboviruses co-circulate.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 会导致急性发热性疾病,并导致 关节痛 衰弱,血清学检测仍然是 诊断 和 监测 的核心。然而,在多种虫媒病毒共同循环的环境中,基于抗体的结果因交叉反应而变得复杂。该综述的重点是共流行环境中的 CHIKV 血清学交叉反应,检查其机制、诊断意义和流行病学后果。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述区分了影响 CHIKV 血清学 的三种相关但不同的现象:生物交叉反应性,由相关病毒之间真正的抗原重叠引起;与检测相关的非目标反应性,其中诊断平台在病毒之间没有建立生物学关系的情况下产生阳性信号;诊断错误分类,将两者混为一谈的下游流行病学后果。将此框架应用于五个病毒对,我们发现CHIKV-O'nyong-nyong病毒(ONNV)、CHIKV-Mayaro病毒(MAYV)和CHIKV-罗斯河病毒(RRV)关系得到了共享的甲病毒抗原结构的支持,并且在一些研究中还得到了功能性交叉中和的支持。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 这些区别很重要:未经调整的血清阳性率可能会夸大或掩盖 CHIKV 传播 的估计值,并且没有一个诊断平台可以解决每个病毒对的问题。我们认为,共流行环境中的 CHIKV 诊断 需要分层策略:急性期进行分子检测,随后进行抗原告知和多重 血清学,以及基于中和的确认(其中归因至关重要),并结合 监测 的交叉反应感知统计模型。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 所提供的证据并未报告关于 CHIKV 与所有相关病毒之间交叉反应机制的具体共识。该综述强调,DENV 和 ZIKV 相关血清中的 CHIKV 反应性缺乏既定的生物学基础,被归类为未解决机制的检测相关非靶标反应性。此外,审查指出,没有一个诊断平台可以解决每个病毒对的问题,这表明当前诊断方法存在差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 加强分析验证和确认性检测,特别是在尼日利亚等 CHIKV、DENV 和相关甲病毒共同传播的非洲地区,对于提高诊断准确性和流行病学推断至关重要。

papers.title: Acute-phase clinical profile and quality of life in patients with chikungunya during the 2025 outbreak in Bangladesh: A facility-based cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bangladesh experienced a notable resurgence of chikungunya cases in 2025, following its last major outbreak in 2017. This study aimed to characterize the epidemiological profile of laboratory-confirmed chikungunya cases in Bangladesh. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included and interviewed 442 laboratory-confirmed adult chikungunya cases. Pain was assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS, 0-10) and quality of life was measured via the validated Bangla EQ-5D-3 L instrument, which evaluates five domains-mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain/discomfort, and anxiety/depression. Overall health was rated using the EQ-VAS, a vertical scale ranging from 0 ("worst imaginable health state") to 100 ("best imaginable health state"). Index scores were derived using the trade-off (TTO) valuation set. Associations with the overall EQ-5D index were analyzed using Tobit regression, whereas domain-specific associations were examined via ordinal logistic regression models. RESULTS: Of all, 16.5% of patients required hospital admission, with a median length of stay of 5 days (IQR 3-6), and the rest of them consulted on an outdoor basis. The mean (SD) age of the participants was 45·3 (15·5) years, and 60% were female. Fever (98%) and arthralgia (97%) were the predominant symptoms. Mild pain was reported by 6% of patients, while 40% had moderate and 54% had severe pain, with a median VAS score of 8.0 (IQR 7.0-9.0). Over 70% of the participants reported mobility limitations, self-care, functional impairment, pain or psychological symptoms. The median EQ-5D index was 0·78 (IQR 0·60-0·96). Female sex (β = -0·10, 95% CI -0·17, -0·02) and greater pain severity (β = -0·26, 95% CI -0·37, -0·15) were independently associated with a lower EQ-5D index. CONCLUSIONS: During the outbreak, chikungunya patients in Bangladesh predominantly presented with fever and joint pain and experienced marked declines in quality of life, with women being disproportionately affected.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the acute-phase clinical profile and quality of life of chikungunya patients during the 2025 outbreak in Bangladesh. It included 442 laboratory-confirmed adult cases and assessed symptoms, pain levels, and quality of life using validated instruments. The study highlights the significant impact of chikungunya on patients' health and the need for targeted interventions. However, the cross-sectional design limits the ability to establish causality, and the findings should be interpreted with caution due to potential biases and confounding factors.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included and interviewed 442 laboratory-confirmed adult chikungunya cases. Pain was assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS, 0-10) and quality of life was measured via the validated Bangla EQ-5D-3 L instrument, which evaluates five domains-mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain/discomfort, and anxiety/depression. Overall health was rated using the EQ-VAS, a vertical scale ranging from 0 ("worst imaginable health state") to 100 ("best imaginable health state"). Index scores were derived using the trade-off (TTO) valuation set. Associations with the overall EQ-5D index were analyzed using Tobit regression, whereas domain-specific associations were examined via ordinal logistic regression models. The mean (SD) age of the participants was 45·3 (15·5) years, and 60% were female. Fever (98%) and arthralgia (97%) were the predominant symptoms. Mild pain was reported by 6% of patients, while 40% had moderate and 54% had severe pain, with a median VAS score of 8.0 (IQR 7.0-9.0). Over 70% of the participants reported mobility limitations, self-care, functional impairment, pain or psychological symptoms. The median EQ-5D index was 0·78 (IQR 0·60-0·96). Female sex (β = -0·10, 95% CI -0·17, -0·02) and greater pain severity (β = -0·26, 95% CI -0·37, -0·15) were independently associated with a lower EQ-5D index. CONCLUSIONS: During the outbreak, chikungunya patients in Bangladesh predominantly presented with fever and joint pain and experienced marked declines in quality of life, with women being disproportionately affected.

papers.title: Divergent climate suitability profiles for dengue and chikungunya transmission by Aedes albopictus in Mauritius
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Empirical surveillance for Aedes -borne arboviruses is inherently reactive, detecting transmission after it has commenced. For small island settings where dengue and chikungunya circulate sporadically, characterising when and where environmental conditions could support local transmission is critical for preparedness. In Mauritius, Aedes albopictus is the sole primary vector for dengue and chikungunya viruses, but previous suitability assessments have relied on Aedes aegypti parameterisation. Methods We estimated monthly Index P for dengue and chikungunya across 160 localities in Mauritius from January 2014 to October 2024. Index P, a mechanistic transmission suitability measure derived from the Ross-Macdonald framework that climate-dependent transmission potential attributable to one adult female mosquito. Mean temperature and relative humidity were derived from ERA5-Land reanalysis dataset via Google Earth Engine and incorporated within the Mosquito-borne Viral Suitability Estimator (MVSE) framework. Index P was also parameterised with Ae. albopictus -specific biological priors and virus-specific vector competence values for both dengue and chikungunya. Results Transmission suitability for both viruses was concentrated within the austral summer (November to April), with near-zero values in winter, below the indicative transmission threshold (Index P ≥ 0.5). Chikungunya exhibited consistently higher, more spatially widespread and longer-lasting suitability than dengue: all districts exceeded the transmission suitability threshold for chikungunya (Index P = 0.71), while median dengue Index P = 0.24, remaining below this threshold, during the same study period. Dengue peak suitability was concentrated in western coastal localities, consistent with the greater thermal sensitivity of its extrinsic incubation period in Ae. Conclusions These findings indicate that dengue and chikungunya have distinct, virus-specific climate-suitability profiles in Mauritius, and should not be treated as interchangeable for preparedness purposes. This provides an important Ae. albopictus -parameterised evidence base for Mauritius, enabling seasonal and geographic targeting of surveillance and vector control ahead of, rather than in response to local transmission.

analysis.main_results: Transmission suitability for both viruses was concentrated during the austral summer (November to April), with near-zero values in winter, below the indicative transmission threshold (Index P ≥ 0.5). elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过描述小岛屿环境中何时何地环境条件可以支持登革热和基孔肯雅热的局部 传播 来解决反应性 监测 的局限性。这一背景凸显了积极做好准备的必要性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究估计了 2014 年 1 月至 2024 年 10 月毛里求斯 160 个地区登革热和基孔肯雅热的月度指数 P。研究重点关注在该地区零星传播的唯一主要 媒介 白纹伊蚊。
elements_zh.methods: 指数 P 是使用 Ross-Macdonald 框架计算的,结合了通过 Google Earth Engine 获得的 ERA5-Land 再分析数据集的平均温度和相对湿度。使用蚊媒病毒适宜性估计器 (MVSE) 框架,其中包含白纹伊蚊特有的参数以及针对登革热和基孔肯雅热的病毒特有的 媒介 能力值。
elements_zh.main_results: 传播 对两种病毒的适宜性集中在南方夏季(11 月至 4 月),冬季值接近于零,低于指示性 传播 阈值(指数 P ≥ 0.5)。基孔肯雅热的适宜性始终高于登革热,在空间上更广泛且持续时间更长,所有地区均超过基孔肯雅热阈值(指数 P = 0.71),而登革热仍低于阈值(中位指数 P = 0.24)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,登革热和基孔肯雅热在毛里求斯具有独特的、特定于病毒的气候适宜性特征,这表明出于防备目的,不应将它们视为可互换的。这一发现为 监测 和 媒介 控制的季节性和地理定位提供了新颖的参数化证据基础。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为毛里求斯制定有针对性的 监测 和 媒介 控制策略提供了依据,从而能够在当地 传播 之前采取主动措施,而不是被动响应。这对于改善小岛屿环境的准备和资源分配具有重要意义。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于气候数据和生物学先验,这可能会带来不确定性。然而,机械框架和病毒特异性参数的使用提供了强有力的证据基础,支持适度的置信度评估。

papers.title: Potential threats of porcine Getah virus outbreaks and its specific antagonism of host antiviral response through proteasome-dependent degradation of P46 by nsP2.
papers.abstract: Alphaviruses are a genus of positive-strand RNA viruses classified in the Togaviridae family. It contains many important human and animal pathogens, such as chikungunya virus (CHIKV), Sindbis virus (SINV), Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV), Semliki Forest virus (SFV) and Ross River virus (RRV), posing significant threats to public health and animal welfare. As a member of genus Alphavirus, porcine Getah virus (GETV) is re-emerging around in many parts of the world in recent years (2022-2025) and has caused small to large-scale outbreaks of diarrhea related diseases in pig industry. In this study, a virulent porcine GETV (JLy1 strain) was isolated from the intestinal contents of diarrheic piglets. analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the potential threats of porcine Getah virus (GETV) outbreaks and its mechanism of antagonizing host antiviral responses. The study found that GETV downregulates the host protein P46, suggesting a regulatory relationship between GETV infection and P46 expression. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨猪盖塔病毒(GETV)暴发的潜在威胁及其拮抗宿主 抗病毒药物反应的机制。包括GETV在内的甲病毒属披膜病毒科正链RNA病毒属,含有许多重要的人类和动物病原体,如基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)、辛德比斯病毒(SINV)、委内瑞拉马脑炎病毒(VEEV)、塞姆利基森林病毒(SFV)和罗斯河病毒(RRV),对公众健康和动物福利构成重大威胁。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及从腹泻仔猪的肠道内容物中分离出强毒力的猪 GETV(JLy1 株)。使用AG129小鼠作为感染模型,所有感染小鼠均死于JLy1感染并伴有严重的肠道损伤。进一步的研究表明,GETV 还会引起 2 日龄仔猪腹泻以及肠、肺和脾损伤,导致 100% 死亡率。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用 AG129 小鼠作为感染模型来评估 GETV 感染的影响。宿主 蛋白 P46 在 GETV 感染的肠道组织中被筛选出下调,表明 GETV 感染与内源性 P46 表达之间存在潜在的调节关系。测试 P46 的异位表达可抑制 GETV 感染,而通过 CRISPR-Cas9 编辑敲除 P46 可促进 GETV 复制。
elements_zh.main_results: 受感染的小鼠死于 JLy1 感染并伴有严重的肠道损伤。GETV 引起 2 日龄仔猪腹泻以及肠、肺和脾损伤,导致 100% 死亡率。筛选出宿主蛋白P46在GETV感染的肠道组织中明显下调。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,P46 作为一种新型 抗病毒药物 调节剂来对抗 GETV 感染。进一步的研究表明,与其他甲病毒(包括 CHIKV、VEEV、SINV、SFV 和 RRV)相比,GETV 采用独特的机制通过 Lys48 连接的蛋白酶体依赖性降解来拮抗 P46 抗病毒药物 反应。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究提供了对重新出现的 GETV 的 暴发 风险和免疫逃避机制的见解,增进了我们对 GETV 发病机制 的理解。这些发现可能为未来开发 GETV 暴发 针对性干预措施的研究提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其使用 AG129 小鼠作为感染模型,可能无法完全代表人类 免疫应答。证据是中等的,因为这些发现是基于体内实验和分子筛查,没有直接的临床或流行病学数据。

papers.title: Chikungunya virus dynamics and persistence in body fluids—Nanning, Guangxi Province, China, 2025
papers.abstract: In 2025, China experienced its largest outbreak of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an acute infectious disease transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes. This study aims to analyze the dynamic changes, developmental trends, and persistence of CHIKV in body fluids, based on infection data collected from Nanning, China. A total of 506 specimens were longitudinally obtained from 53 hospitalized patients in Nanning, China. Positivity rates among different specimen types were compared using the Chi-square test or Fisher’s exact test, while the Kruskal-Wallis test was applied to evaluate differences in cycle threshold (Ct) values. To estimate the probability of viral detection, generalized estimating equations (GEE) were employed, and parametric survival analysis was conducted to examine the duration of viral persistence in human body fluids. Serum had the highest positivity rate (81.20%), followed by plasma (72.50%), while urine (4.73%) and saliva (11.03%) were much lower. In the first four days following the onset of symptoms, the median Ct values for serum and plasma were lower compared to those for saliva and urine. According to GEE analysis, saliva showed the quickest decline in the likelihood of a positive test result, decreasing from 52.2% on day 1 to just 0.7% by day 7. Serum and plasma followed, with positivity rates dropping from over 85% on day 3 to around 30% by day 7. Urine consistently had low positivity rates and did not show a statistically significant relationship with the number of days since symptoms began. Parametric survival analysis indicated similar median durations of serum (5.8 days, 95% CI : 4.8–6.9) and plasma (5.8 days, 95% CI : 4.7–7.1), while saliva had a shorter median duration of 3.5 days (95% CI : 3.0–4.1). Urine was not included in this analysis due to an insufficient number of positive samples. Blood is the preferred sample for detecting the chikungunya virus and accurately assessing the duration of the virus in the body; additionally, compared to urine, saliva is more sensitive for detecting the virus during the acute phase of the disease, which is important for subsequent transmission and public health control measures.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及中国南宁市的 53 名住院患者,纵向采集了 506 份标本来检查 CHIKV 动态。由于阳性样本数量不足,尿液被排除。

Serum had the highest positivity rate (81.20%), followed by plasma (72.50%), while urine (4.73%) and saliva (11.03%) were much lower. In the first four days following the onset of symptoms, the median Ct values for serum and plasma were lower compared to those for saliva and urine. According to GEE analysis, saliva showed the quickest decline in the likelihood of a positive test result, decreasing from 52.2% on day 1 to just 0.7% by day 7. Serum and plasma followed, with positivity rates dropping from over 85% on day 3 to around 30% by day 7. Urine consistently had low positivity rates and did not show a statistically significant relationship with the number of days since symptoms began. Parametric survival analysis indicated similar median durations of serum (5.8 days, 95% CI : 4.8–6.9) and plasma (5.8 days, 95% CI : 4.7–7.1), while saliva had a shorter median duration of 3.5 days (95% CI : 3.0–4.1). Urine was not included in this analysis due to an insufficient number of positive samples. Blood is the preferred sample for detecting the chikungunya virus and accurately assessing the duration of the virus in the body; additionally, compared to urine, saliva is more sensitive for detecting the virus during the acute phase of the disease, which is important for subsequent transmission and public health control measures.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在分析2025年中国最大规模基孔肯雅热暴发后,基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)在体液中的动态变化、发展趋势及持续时间。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及中国南宁市的 53 名住院患者,纵向采集了 506 份标本来检查 CHIKV 动态。由于阳性样本数量不足,尿液被排除。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究采用卡方检验或Fisher精确检验比较不同标本类型的阳性率,并应用Kruskal-Wallis检验评估循环阈值(Ct值)差异。采用广义估计方程(GEE)估计病毒检出概率,并进行参数生存分析以评估病毒在人体体液中的持续时间。
analysis_zh.main_results: 血清的阳性率最高(81.20%),其次为血浆(72.50%),尿液(4.73%)和唾液(11.03%)的阳性率明显较低。在症状出现后的前四天内,血清和血浆的中位Ct值低于唾液和尿液。唾液的阳性检出概率下降最快,从第1天的52.2%降至第7天的0.7%。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,血清和血浆在基孔肯雅病毒检测及评估其在体内持续时间方面更为有效,而唾液在疾病急性期的检测敏感性更高。这些结果有助于理解病毒行为并改进公共卫生控制措施。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究为基孔肯雅病毒最佳标本类型的选择提供了关键依据,并强调了在疾病急性期进行唾液检测的重要性,以提高诊断效率并加强疾病控制。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于阳性样本不足,该研究受到尿液排除的限制,这可能会影响分析的完整性。证据强度适中,因为结果基于单个 暴发,可能无法完全推广。

papers.title: Chikungunya in older people: a guide for primary care nurses
papers.abstract: Chikungunya is a mosquito-borne viral infection with an expanding global spread, driven by climate change and increased international travel, leading to more older people and people with long-term health conditions travelling abroad. Chikungunya is characterised by sudden-onset fever and severe joint pain; however, older adults may present atypically, with milder or absent fever and non-specific symptoms, increasing the risk of delayed diagnosis. Pre-travel advice, vaccination and mosquito bite avoidance are key for prevention. This article discusses the epidemiology of chikungunya, differences in clinical presentation between age groups, diagnostic approaches and key considerations for management and prevention.

analysis.summary_en: Chikungunya is a mosquito-borne viral infection with expanding global spread, driven by climate change and increased international travel, particularly among older people and those with long-term health conditions (A1). It typically causes sudden-onset fever and severe joint pain, but older adults may present atypically with milder or absent fever and non-specific symptoms, raising the risk of delayed diagnosis (A2). The available material is a practice-nursing review article rather than an empirical study, so no primary design, sample, assays or statistics are reported (A4). Key prevention messages emphasised are pre-travel advice, vaccination and mosquito bite avoidance (A3). The review synthesises epidemiology, age-related clinical differences, diagnostic considerations and management/prevention priorities relevant to primary care nurses (A4). Evidence is limited to narrative guidance without primary data, and confidence in any quantitative conclusion is therefore low.

papers.title: Perfil epidemiológico da Chikungunya em um município no sul do da Bahia, de 2016 a 2024
papers.abstract: Objetivo: Analisar o perfil epidemiológico da febre Chikungunya no município de Itabuna, Bahia, entre 2016 e 2024, com ênfase em variáveis sociodemográficas, manifestações clínicas e critérios diagnósticos. Métodos: Estudo descritivo e retrospectivo baseado em dados do Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação (SINAN). Foram analisados casos notificados no período, com seleção de registros confirmados por critérios laboratoriais ou clínico-epidemiológicos após limpeza dos dados. Variáveis sociodemográficas, clínicas, comorbidades e desfechos foram avaliadas por estatística descritiva, teste qui-quadrado e regressão logística univariada (p<0,05). Resultados: Foram notificados 18.211 casos suspeitos, dos quais 5.309 (29,2%) foram confirmados. Predominaram casos em mulheres (63,9%), residentes da área urbana (89,5%) e confirmação clínico-epidemiológica (70,7%). Os sintomas mais frequentes foram artralgia (72,9%), febre (67,6%) e mialgia (60,4%). Houve pico de casos em 2016 e novo aumento em 2023. Observou-se alta incompletude em variáveis como raça e escolaridade e baixa realização de sorologia. Conclusão: O perfil indica maior acometimento feminino e urbano, além de fragilidades na vigilância epidemiológica local, demandando melhorias no SINAN e no fluxo diagnóstico para políticas locais mais eficazes.
authors: Íris Terezinha Santos de Santana Silva

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to analyze the epidemiological profile of Chikungunya virus in Itabuna, Bahia, from 2016 to 2024, focusing on sociodemographic variables, clinical manifestations and diagnostic criteria.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a descriptive and retrospective study based on data from the SINAN system, analyzing cases notified during the period, with data cleaning and selection of confirmed cases through laboratory or clinical-epidemiological criteria.
analysis.methods: Sociodemographic, clinical, comorbidity and outcome variables were evaluated using descriptive statistics, chi-square test and univariate logistic regression (p<0.05).
analysis.main_results: A total of 18,211 suspected cases were reported, of which 5,309 (29.2%) were confirmed. The majority of cases were in women (63.9%), residents of urban areas (89.5%) and confirmed through clinical-epidemiological criteria (70.7%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight a higher prevalence among women and urban populations, and underscore weaknesses in local epidemiological surveillance, suggesting the need for improvements in SINAN and diagnostic flow for more effective local policies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results can inform targeted surveillance and diagnostic strategies in urban areas, particularly for women, and highlight the importance of strengthening the SINAN system for better disease control.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: There was incomplete data on variables such as race and education level, and low serology performance, which may limit the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the epidemiological profile of Chikungunya virus in Itabuna, Bahia, from 2016 to 2024, focusing on sociodemographic variables, clinical manifestations and diagnostic criteria. It was a descriptive and retrospective study based on SINAN data, with confirmed cases selected through laboratory or clinical-epidemiological criteria. The study found that 29.2% of 18,211 suspected cases were confirmed, with a higher prevalence among women and urban residents. The results indicated a predominance of clinical-epidemiological confirmation and highlighted weaknesses in local surveillance. The findings suggest the need for improved diagnostic flow and surveillance in urban areas, particularly for women. However, the study had limitations, including incomplete data on race and education and low serology performance, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is considered moderate due to these limitations.

Predominaram casos em mulheres (63,9%), residentes da área urbana (89,5%) e confirmação clínico-epidemiológica (70,7%). papers.title: Neglected arboviruses in South America: clinical manifestations and diagnostic challenges.
papers.abstract: In South America, the arboviruses that are most noted are those that lead to dengue, Zika, and chikungunya. Nevertheless, there are additional arboviruses that trigger outbreaks, yet do not receive adequate attention, including Oropouche virus (OROV), Mayaro virus (MAYV), Saint Louis Encephalitis virus, Madariaga virus (MADV), and Rocío virus (ROCV). A rapid review was conducted using the databases PubMed, LILACS, Scopus, and Google Scholar. This analysis focused on studies that outline the clinical signs and diagnostic methods of neglected arboviruses impacting human populations in South America. A total of 38 studies met the inclusion criteria. Most reports focused on OROV and MAYV, whereas only a few studies described MADV and ROCV. Brazil accounted for the largest proportion of studies, followed by Peru. Across the reviewed literature, these arboviruses were associated with a broad clinical spectrum, ranging from non-specific febrile illness to severe neurological disease and congenital complications. Diagnostic approaches included serological assays, viral isolation or neutralization tests, and molecular methods such as RT-PCR. The increasing spread of these under-reported arboviruses in South America requires strengthening monitoring systems, optimizing access to specific diagnostics, and training healthcare personnel to identify these infections early and manage them appropriately.
papers.journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 对 38 项研究进行了快速审查,以评估影响南美洲人群的被忽视的虫媒病毒的临床症状和诊断方法。
analysis_zh.methods: 该综述包括利用血清学测定、病毒分离或中和试验以及 RT-PCR 等分子方法来评估这些虫媒病毒的临床和诊断方面的研究。
analysis_zh.main_results: 巴西在研究数量中占比最高,其次为秘鲁。综述文献显示,这些虫媒病毒可引发广泛的临床谱系,从非特异性发热疾病到严重神经系统疾病及先天性并发症。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者指出,这些虫媒病毒报告不足的特性凸显了改善监测与诊断能力的必要性,因其可引发多样化的临床结局。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了加强监测系统与提升诊断工具的重要性,以更好地管理和预防南美被忽视虫媒病毒的传播。

papers.title: Effects of different X-ray irradiation dosages on Wolbachia trans-infected and uninfected Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Aedes aegypti is a primary vector of several arboviral diseases, including dengue, chikungunya, Zika, and yellow fever. aegypti can disrupt virus transmission cycles, thereby reducing the incidence of these diseases. Releasing sterile Ae. aegypti males has been implemented to suppress their natural populations, using three approaches, i.e., ionizing radiation-induced sterilization (Sterile Insect Technique, SIT), Wolbachia-induced cytoplasmic incompatibility (Incompatible Insect Technique, IIT), and a combination of both approaches (SIT/IIT). METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: This study investigated effects of different X-ray radiation doses on the ecological fitness of the Thai wild-type and Wolbachia trans-infected Ae. Both wild-type and wAlbB trans-infected Ae. aegypti were irradiated with different X-ray radiation dosages, i.e., 30, 50, and 70 Gy, at the pupal stage. Our results demonstrated reduced fitness parameters in both Ae. aegypti strains when irradiation dosages increased, with greater adverse effects observed in the Wolbachia-infected group. Interestingly, 30 Gy irradiation appeared to prolong the lifespan of wAlbB trans-infected Ae. Male fertility in both wild-type and wAlbB trans-infected mosquitoes irradiated at 50 Gy and 70 Gy was nearly zero. Wolbachia density generally declined with increasing radiation, and higher doses were associated with reduced mating competitiveness. At 30 Gy, wild-type males outperformed wAlbB trans-infected males in mating competitiveness; but it was reversed at 50 Gy and 70 Gy. CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: Based on the evaluation of ecological fitness parameters and mating competitiveness across various X-ray dosages under laboratory conditions, 30 Gy is recommended for sterilizing both Thai wild-type and wAlbB trans-infected Ae. Our findings aim to improve the efficiency of sterile mosquito release programs, thereby suppressing Ae. aegypti vector populations and mitigating the risk of arboviral disease transmission.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of different X-ray irradiation dosages on the ecological fitness of Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, which are primary vectors of several arboviral diseases, including chikungunya.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in a laboratory setting, where both wild-type and Wolbachia trans-infected Aedes aegypti mosquitoes were irradiated with dosages of 30, 50, and 70 Gy at the pupal stage. The research focused on assessing the impact of these dosages on mosquito fitness and mating competitiveness.
analysis.methods: The study used X-ray irradiation at different dosages to assess the ecological fitness of Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. It evaluated parameters such as lifespan, mating competitiveness, and Wolbachia density in both wild-type and trans-infected strains under controlled laboratory conditions.
analysis.main_results: The results showed that increased X-ray dosages led to reduced fitness parameters in both mosquito strains, with greater adverse effects observed in the Wolbachia-infected group. At 30 Gy, wild-type males outperformed Wolbachia-infected males in mating competitiveness, but this was reversed at 50 Gy and 70 Gy. Wolbachia density generally declined with higher radiation doses, and mating competitiveness was reduced at higher doses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that 30 Gy is the optimal dosage for sterilizing both wild-type and Wolbachia-infected Aedes aegypti mosquitoes under laboratory conditions, which could enhance the efficiency of sterile mosquito release programs for disease suppression.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings could inform the development of more effective sterile mosquito release programs to suppress Aedes aegypti populations and reduce the transmission of chikungunya and other arboviral diseases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted under laboratory conditions, which may not fully reflect real-world ecological dynamics. The evidence is moderate, as the results are based on controlled experiments rather than field observations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the effects of different X-ray irradiation dosages on the ecological fitness of Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, which are primary vectors of chikungunya and other arboviral diseases. The research focused on assessing how varying dosages of 30, 50, and 70 Gy impact mosquito lifespan, mating competitiveness, and Wolbachia density in both wild-type and trans-infected strains. Results indicated that higher dosages reduced fitness parameters more significantly in Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes, with 30 Gy being the optimal for sterilization. The authors concluded that these findings could improve sterile mosquito release programs to suppress vector populations and mitigate disease transmission. However, the study was limited to laboratory conditions, which may not fully represent real-world scenarios, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

papers.title_zh: 不同X射线照射剂量对转染和未感染沃尔巴克氏体的埃及伊蚊的影响
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Aedes aegypti is a primary vector of several arboviral diseases, including dengue, chikungunya, Zika, and yellow fever. aegypti can disrupt virus transmission cycles, thereby reducing the incidence of these diseases. Releasing sterile Ae. aegypti males has been implemented to suppress their natural populations, using three approaches, i.e., ionizing radiation-induced sterilization (Sterile Insect Technique, SIT), Wolbachia-induced cytoplasmic incompatibility (Incompatible Insect Technique, IIT), and a combination of both approaches (SIT/IIT). METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: This study investigated effects of different X-ray radiation doses on the ecological fitness of the Thai wild-type and Wolbachia trans-infected Ae. Both wild-type and wAlbB trans-infected Ae. aegypti were irradiated with different X-ray radiation dosages, i.e., 30, 50, and 70 Gy, at the pupal stage. Our results demonstrated reduced fitness parameters in both Ae. aegypti strains when irradiation dosages increased, with greater adverse effects observed in the Wolbachia-infected group. Interestingly, 30 Gy irradiation appeared to prolong the lifespan of wAlbB trans-infected Ae. Male fertility in both wild-type and wAlbB trans-infected mosquitoes irradiated at 50 Gy and 70 Gy was nearly zero. Wolbachia density generally declined with increasing radiation, and higher doses were associated with reduced mating competitiveness. At 30 Gy, wild-type males outperformed wAlbB trans-infected males in mating competitiveness; but it was reversed at 50 Gy and 70 Gy. CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: Based on the evaluation of ecological fitness parameters and mating competitiveness across various X-ray dosages under laboratory conditions, 30 Gy is recommended for sterilizing both Thai wild-type and wAlbB trans-infected Ae. Our findings aim to improve the efficiency of sterile mosquito release programs, thereby suppressing Ae. aegypti vector populations and mitigating the risk of arboviral disease transmission.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:埃及伊蚊是多种虫媒病毒疾病的主要 媒介,包括登革热、基孔肯雅热、寨卡病毒和黄热病。埃及伊蚊可以破坏病毒发病率周期,从而减少这些疾病的发病率。释放无菌Ae。已使用三种方法来抑制埃及雄性埃及伊蚊的自然种群,即电离辐射诱导的绝育(不育昆虫技术,SIT)、沃尔巴克氏体诱导的细胞质不相容性(不相容昆虫技术,IIT)以及两种方法的组合(SIT/IIT)。方法/主要发现:本研究调查了不同 X 射线辐射剂量对泰国野生型和沃尔巴克氏体反式感染伊蚊生态适应性的影响。野生型和 wAlbB 均转染伊蚊。埃及伊蚊在蛹期接受不同剂量的X射线照射,即30、50和70 Gy。我们的结果表明,两种 Ae 的适应度参数均有所降低。当辐照剂量增加时,埃及菌株受到影响,在沃尔巴克氏体感染组中观察到更大的不良反应。有趣的是,30 Gy 照射似乎可以延长 wAlbB 反式感染的伊蚊的寿命。在 50 Gy 和 70 Gy 照射下,野生型和 wAlbB 反式感染蚊子的雄性生育力几乎为零。沃尔巴克氏体密度通常随着辐射的增加而下降,而较高的剂量与交配竞争力的降低有关。在 30 Gy 时,野生型雄性在交配竞争力方面优于 wAlbB 反式感染的雄性;但在 50 Gy 和 70 Gy 时则相反。结论/意义:根据实验室条件下不同 X 射线剂量的生态适应性参数和交配竞争力评估,建议使用 30 Gy 对泰国野生型和 wAlbB 反式感染的伊蚊进行灭菌。我们的研究结果旨在提高蚊子无菌释放计划的效率,从而抑制伊蚊。埃及伊蚊 媒介 种群并降低虫媒病毒病 传播 的风险。

papers.title: Etiological Spectrum of Acute Febrile Illness in a Tertiary Care Hospital in Assam, India: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Introduction: Acute Febrile Illness (AFI) encompasses a spectrum of conditions marked by fever, often caused by various infectious agents. The aetiological diversity poses challenges in diagnosis and treatment, particularly in regions with limited diagnostic resources. Aim: To evaluate the spectrum of pathogens causing AFI with or without rash in patients. Materials and Methods: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from January 2024 to December 2024 on 1,544 patients who had attended Lakhimpur Medical College and Hospital, North Lakhimpur, Assam, India. Patients with fever (≥ 37.5°C) with or without rash were enrolled. Serological investigations for Measles, Rubella, Dengue, Varicella-zoster, Chikungunya viruses, Japanese Encephalitis (JE), Orientia tsutsugamushi, Leptospira, and Hepatitis viruses were performed using Enzyme-linked Immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and Rapid Detection Testing (RDT) kits. Data analysis was performed using both descriptive and inferential methods. A p-value of <0.05 was considered significant. Results: Fever was prevalent in all 1,544 (100%) cases, followed by 856 (55.44%) cases of headache, 636 (41.19%) with cough, 476 (30.83%) with vomiting, 347 (22.47%) with abdominal pain, 59 (3.82%) cases with dysentery, 52 (3.37%) with diarrhoea, 46 (2.98%) cases with unconsciousness, and 21 (1.36%) cases presented with rash. Fever was observed in combination with headache in 856 (55.44%), with cough in 636 (41.19%), with bodyache in 481 (31.15%), and with vomiting in 476 (30.83%) cases. The study identified seasonal variations in infection rates, with peaks during the monsoon months. The majority of positive cases were attributed to Scrub Typhus 133/817 (16.28%), followed by Leptospirosis 129/473 (27.27%), Dengue 84/1273 (6.59%), and JE 20/87 (22.99%), while some had co-infection. Conclusion: The study underscores the importance of integrated clinical and laboratory approaches in diagnosing AFI. Scrub typhus, leptospirosis, and dengue were identified as major causes, emphasising the need for enhanced surveillance and diagnostic capabilities.
papers.journal: Journal of Clinical and Diagnostic Research

papers.title_zh: 印度阿萨姆邦一家三级护理医院急性发热性疾病的病因学谱:一项横断面研究
papers.source_body_en: Introduction: Acute Febrile Illness (AFI) encompasses a spectrum of conditions marked by fever, often caused by various infectious agents. The aetiological diversity poses challenges in diagnosis and treatment, particularly in regions with limited diagnostic resources. Aim: To evaluate the spectrum of pathogens causing AFI with or without rash in patients. Materials and Methods: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from January 2024 to December 2024 on 1,544 patients who had attended Lakhimpur Medical College and Hospital, North Lakhimpur, Assam, India. Patients with fever (≥ 37.5°C) with or without rash were enrolled. Serological investigations for Measles, Rubella, Dengue, Varicella-zoster, Chikungunya viruses, Japanese Encephalitis (JE), Orientia tsutsugamushi, Leptospira, and Hepatitis viruses were performed using Enzyme-linked Immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and Rapid Detection Testing (RDT) kits. Data analysis was performed using both descriptive and inferential methods. A p-value of <0.05 was considered significant. Results: Fever was prevalent in all 1,544 (100%) cases, followed by 856 (55.44%) cases of headache, 636 (41.19%) with cough, 476 (30.83%) with vomiting, 347 (22.47%) with abdominal pain, 59 (3.82%) cases with dysentery, 52 (3.37%) with diarrhoea, 46 (2.98%) cases with unconsciousness, and 21 (1.36%) cases presented with rash. Fever was observed in combination with headache in 856 (55.44%), with cough in 636 (41.19%), with bodyache in 481 (31.15%), and with vomiting in 476 (30.83%) cases. The study identified seasonal variations in infection rates, with peaks during the monsoon months. The majority of positive cases were attributed to Scrub Typhus 133/817 (16.28%), followed by Leptospirosis 129/473 (27.27%), Dengue 84/1273 (6.59%), and JE 20/87 (22.99%), while some had co-infection. Conclusion: The study underscores the importance of integrated clinical and laboratory approaches in diagnosing AFI. Scrub typhus, leptospirosis, and dengue were identified as major causes, emphasising the need for enhanced surveillance and diagnostic capabilities.
papers.abstract_zh: 简介:急性发热性疾病 (AFI) 涵盖一系列以发烧为特征的病症,通常由各种传染源引起。病因多样性给 诊断 和 治疗 带来了挑战,特别是在诊断资源有限的地区。目的:评估引起 AFI(伴或不伴皮疹)患者的病原体谱。材料和方法:2024 年 1 月至 2024 年 12 月,对印度阿萨姆邦北拉金布尔拉金布尔医学院和医院就诊的 1,544 名患者进行了一项以医院为基础的横断面研究。发热(≥ 37.5°C)伴或不伴皮疹的患者纳入研究。使用酶联免疫吸附测定 (ELISA) 和快速检测测试 (RDT) 试剂盒对麻疹、风疹、登革热、水痘带状疱疹、基孔肯雅病毒、日本脑炎 (JE)、恙虫病东方体、钩端螺旋体和肝炎病毒进行血清学研究。使用描述性和推理性方法进行数据分析。p 值 <0.05 被认为是显着的。结果:1544例(100%)患者中,以发热为主,其次为头痛856例(55.44%),咳嗽636例(41.19%),呕吐476例(30.83%),腹痛347例(22.47%),腹泻59例(3.82%),腹泻52例(3.37%)。腹泻,意识不清 46 例(2.98%),皮疹 21 例(1.36%)。发热伴头痛856例(55.44%),伴咳嗽636例(41.19%),伴全身疼痛481例(31.15%),伴呕吐476例(30.83%)。该研究确定了感染率的季节性变化,在季风月份达到峰值。大多数阳性病例归因于恙虫病133/817(16.28%),其次是钩端螺旋体病129/473(27.27%),登革热84/1273(6.59%)和乙型脑炎20/87(22.99%),还有一些合并感染。结论:该研究强调了综合临床和实验室方法在诊断 AFI 中的重要性。恙虫病、钩端螺旋体病和登革热被确定为主要原因,强调需要增强 监测 和诊断能力。

papers.title: An Overview of Common and Emerging Viral Infections in Humans
papers.abstract: Human life coexists with all other living organisms, ranging from microorganisms to other animals in the ecosystem. Infectious agents can affect the ecosystem’s coherence and remain a significant challenge to human life. Among these, some viruses cause mild infections, while others can have fatal impacts on human life worldwide. Self-acquired genetic variations of viruses pose a significant challenge to efficient control and can trigger severe impacts on human health. The rapid evolution of viruses leads to the emergence of hitherto unknown drug-resistant strains. The current era has witnessed the emergence of several deadly viral infections, such as Corona, Nipah, Ebola, and Zika. Each of these outbreaks underscores the importance of comprehensive research into the improvement of diagnosis, surveillance, treatment, and prevention of the deadliest viral infections. The present chapter outlines viral diseases; Corona, Chikungunya, Ebola, Influenza, and Zika virus infections were selected as representative emerging diseases for detailed discussion.

papers.source_body_en: Human life coexists with all other living organisms, ranging from microorganisms to other animals in the ecosystem. Infectious agents can affect the ecosystem’s coherence and remain a significant challenge to human life. Among these, some viruses cause mild infections, while others can have fatal impacts on human life worldwide. Self-acquired genetic variations of viruses pose a significant challenge to efficient control and can trigger severe impacts on human health. The rapid evolution of viruses leads to the emergence of hitherto unknown drug-resistant strains. The current era has witnessed the emergence of several deadly viral infections, such as Corona, Nipah, Ebola, and Zika. Each of these outbreaks underscores the importance of comprehensive research into the improvement of diagnosis, surveillance, treatment, and prevention of the deadliest viral infections. The present chapter outlines viral diseases; Corona, Chikungunya, Ebola, Influenza, and Zika virus infections were selected as representative emerging diseases for detailed discussion.

news.rss_summary_html: New vaccine strategy protects mice against chikungunya  European Animal Research Association

news.content_title: EARA | News - New vaccine strategy protects mice against chikungunya
news.content: Why animal research?PolicyTransparency NewsEventsProjectsMembershipAbout EARA New vaccine strategy protects mice against chikungunya Author Nuno Goncalves Back to news list Research from Brazil and Germany has developed a new vaccine approach that protected mice against chikungunya after a single dose and could potentially be adapted to target other viruses. Chikungunya is a mosquito-borne viral disease that causes fever and severe joint pain and has been reported in over 110 countries. There is no vaccine, and treatments exclusively address symptoms. Research from the University of São Paulo (USP) and the University of Bonn genetically modified the chikungunya virus to trigger an immune response upon infection while preventing further cell infection, a challenge in traditional attenuated-virus vaccines. In mice genetically altered to be particularly vulnerable to viral infections, a single dose protected against an otherwise lethal chikungunya infection. When tested in mice with a normal immune system, it reduced virus levels in the blood and swelling in the feet—a sign of the joint inflammation caused by chikungunya. The modified vaccine also produced antibodies capable of neutralising Mayaro virus, a related mosquito-borne virus. Danillo Lucas Alves Esposito, from the University of São Paulo and the University of Bonn and first author of the study published in npj Vaccines, said about the vaccine: “It’s an interesting platform. Now, in addition to moving forward with clinical trials, we’re interested in using this vaccine platform for other arboviruses.” Chikungunya virus. news.content: Thank you for registering Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in Jump to content Open full menu US Edition UK EditionAsia EditionEdición en Español Log in Log in News Sports Culture Lifestyle Money Travel Premium Climate More Swipe for next article Travel News & Advice Chikungunya virus: Expert gives travel advice as France reports summer cases Health authorities have urged people to take precautions against mosquito bites when travelling Copy link Bookmark 3Comments Go to comments Bookmark popover Removed from bookmarks Close popover open image in gallery Two chikungunya vaccines are available in the UK. Here’s what to know after cases have been reported in France (Getty Images) French authorities are promoting mosquito-borne disease prevention after identifying an uptick in August of cases of chikungunya, a virus that causes a sudden onset of fever and joint pain. Three towns in France have reported cases of locally acquired chikungunya this year, with the latest one recorded as recently as 12 August, bringing the total cases up to 25 – however, this is significantly lower than the number recorded last year. The yearly total number of French cases remained at 15 until August, when 10 new cases were identified, according to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC). In response, affected French towns such as Prignac-et-Marcamps have deployed mosquito control teams to try to treat potential stagnant water breeding sites, and the mayor has temporarily banned outdoor sports activities. Other towns in the Paris, Toulouse, Gironde and Tarn regions have also carried out mosquito-control operations, such as spraying areas with insecticide mist. While France is the only country in Europe with locally acquired cases, other destinations across the world are still tackling larger outbreaks. RECOMMENDED Dolly Parton had no kids. Here’s where her fortune is going Undo Flight attendant warns against wearing shorts or skirts on a plane Undo Senior Drivers In Washington Did Not See This ComingConsumer Auto Alerts | SponsoredSponsored Undo Squirt Some Honey On Your Dog’s Tongue, Here’s What HappensPets Daily Health | SponsoredSponsored Undo Here is what travellers need to know about the virus, plus advice from a medical specialist on how to best prepare for travelling overseas. What is chikungunya and how is it spread? Chikungunya virus disease (CHIKVD) is a mosquito-borne disease that is found across tropical and sub-tropical regions. It is spread to humans by a bite from an infected mosquito. It cannot be passed from human to human. For cases to become locally acquired, an uninfected mosquito usually feeds on a person who has chikungunya circulating in their blood, usually someone who caught the virus and then returned to their country. The virus then replicates in the mosquito and can be transmitted to a new human when the mosquito bites them. Cases have been found in the Americas, Africa, Asia and Europe. Brazil has had the most cases in 2025 and in 2026. Where are the chikungunya cases? Since the start of 2026, France is the only EU country that has reported local acquired cases of chikungunya, with 25 cases. This is relatively low compared to the same period last year, which saw 154 locally acquired cases by August, and 809 locally acquired cases in mainland France throughout 2025. As of 19 August, 16 of the locally acquired cases were identified in Gironde’s Prignac-et-Marcamps, with the cluster still “active”. The latest case was recorded as recently as 12 August. One case was recorded in Saint-Médard-en-Jalles, also in Gironde, but this cluster was closed after it was deemed an isolated event in June, with no more people reporting having the disease. The other eight cases have been recorded in Saint-Amans-Soult in Tarn, with the cluster still active despite the last case being recorded on 25 July. There have been 110 imported cases to France so far this year, too. Outside the EU, there have been 219,522 confirmed chikungunya cases and 81 associated deaths detected in 25 countries in 2026. What are the symptoms? Chikungunya originates from a word used by the Makonde people in Tanzania, where the disease was first discovered in the 1950s. It means “that which bends up”, describing the contorted posture of infected people who experience severe joint pain. Alongside joint pain, people can also experience an abrupt onset of fever, joint swelling, muscle pain, headaches, nausea, fatigue and rashes. The joint pain can be debilitating and usually lasts for a few days, but it has been known to last for weeks, months or even years. open image in gallery Réunion recorded over 54,550 confirmed cases during a 2025 outbreak (AFP/Getty) If an infected person does not experience joint pain, the symptoms will be mild and can go unrecognised as chikungunya. Most people will recover fully from the infection. There have been some occasional cases of eye, heart, and neurological complications, while newborns and older people with underlying medical conditions are at a higher risk of severe disease. Patients with severe disease should be hospitalised because of the risk of organ damage or death. Once someone has recovered from chikungunya, they are likely to be immune to future chikungunya infections. Is there a vaccine? Two chikungunya vaccines are available in the UK, containing a form of the virus that has been weakened so it cannot multiply. It works by training the immune system to recognise the virus, which will then produce specific antibodies to attack it. It can only be obtained via a prescription and given to those who plan to travel abroad where the virus is present. One vaccine is available for individuals aged 18 to 59 years, and another for those over 12. Hilary Kirkbride, head of travel health at UKHSA, says: “Simple steps, such as using insect repellent, covering exposed skin and sleeping under insecticide-treated bed nets, can effectively reduce the risk. “Before you travel, check the TravelHealthPro website for the latest health advice on your destination. A chikungunya vaccine may also be considered for those travelling to higher-risk regions.” A travel doctor’s guide to being prepared Dr Richard Dawood, a travel medical specialist at Fleet Street Clinic, explained to the Independent how the vaccination can help travellers prevent getting sick from the chikungunya virus. He said: “This is a new situation for us. Until a very short time ago, we had no vaccine, and the only approach to prevention was to make careful use of insect repellents and insect precautions. “So now we've got this extra tool in the armoury, and because the vaccine gives long-lasting protection, it’s something that could be considered if you are planning to travel over a period of time. “It's a fairly expensive vaccine, but if you’re going to be travelling over a period of years to southern Europe and beyond, it may be something that could be considered.” Wherever you are travelling, Mr Dawood advised holidaymakers to “do your homework”. He said, “If there's an actual outbreak at your destination, then I would say no hesitation, definitely have the vaccine. “Taking a bit of time and getting some really focused travel health advice for your particular trip is very worthwhile because it can save you from getting a vaccine that you don't need or that may not be sensible for you, and it can help prioritise the really important things for your trip.” RECOMMENDED Dolly Parton had a two-word answer to the secret of her lasting marriage Undo What drove the deadly Grand Canyon flooding? news.content: 🌍 Your Global Travel News Source AboutContactPrivacy Policy ☰ NEWS Travel NewsAirline NewsAirlines ✈️Hotel NewsCruise NewsDestinationsTravel DealsTravel Alerts Home✈️ Airline HubsTravel NewsTourism NewsAirline NewsTravel Association NewsRailway NewsCruise NewsDestination NewsHotel NewsMeeting and Event IndustryTravel AlertTravel DealsTravel Trends and FocusTechnology NewsTravel Events NewsAboutContact Home›travel news›France Issues 2026 Chikungunya Alert for Southern Regions Amid Rising Local Transmission travel news France Issues 2026 Chikungunya Alert for Southern Regions Amid Rising Local Transmission France has activated heightened chikungunya vigilance for 2026, specifically targeting southern regions where locally acquired cases and tiger mosquito activity have intensified. By Kunal K Choudhary August 27, 2026 3 min read Image generated by AI France has activated heightened chikungunya vigilance for 2026, focusing on southern regions as locally acquired cases emerge and tiger mosquito activity intensifies. Public health agencies have raised the alert level for the 2026 mosquito season, citing an elevated risk of local transmission in southern territories. These areas, which are primary hubs for summer tourism, are seeing a rise in autochthonous (locally transmitted) infections. According to European monitoring from the ECDC, France is currently the only European nation to report locally acquired chikungunya virus disease in 2026. These cases are concentrated entirely within mainland territories. Surveillance and Case Trends Data from Santé publique France, updated in August 2026, confirms several clusters of local transmission since the start of the season. This follows a significant spike in 2025, during which hundreds of locally acquired cases were documented, primarily in the south. While 2026 case numbers currently remain below the 2025 peak, the year is still tracking as one of the most active periods for mosquito-borne viruses. Health experts warn that even low confirmed case counts can indicate widespread exposure when the mosquito vector is established in residential zones. High-Risk Zones: The Mediterranean Corridor The 2026 alert focuses heavily on southern France, where the invasive tiger mosquito (Aedes albopictus) has been established for over a decade. Historical data shows that most local episodes since 2010 have occurred in: Provence Alpes Côte d’Azur: The most affected region in mainland France, characterized by dense urban areas and warm temperatures. Occitanie: A high-risk zone with significant mosquito habitats. Mediterranean Corridor: Neighboring regions bordering the coast and lower river valleys. The south acts as a gateway for imported infections. Surveillance from 2025 and early 2026 shows a high volume of imported cases linked to travel from tropical areas and La Réunion, which frequently trigger local outbreaks when tiger mosquito populations are high. The Vector: Aedes albopictus Expansion The risk is driven by the spread of the tiger mosquito, which transmits chikungunya, dengue, and Zika. National health insurance data indicates a clear south-to-north gradient of risk. Climate variability is accelerating this trend. Warmer temperatures are extending the breeding season and improving mosquito survival rates. Analysis shows that populations can rebound rapidly after rainfall, maintaining virus circulation through late summer and into early autumn. Critical Guidance for Travelers Visitors to the French Riviera, Provence, and Occitanie should integrate mosquito protection into their travel planning. While there is no routine vaccination recommended for France, there is also no specific, widely deployed treatment for the virus. Preventive Measures: Repellents: Use products containing DEET or picaridin. Clothing: Wear long sleeves and trousers in high-risk areas. Accommodation: Prioritize rentals with air conditioning or window screens. Source Reduction: Empty standing water from containers at villas, campsites, or rural rentals to eliminate breeding sites. Public Health Response Strategy The 2026 strategy employs a combined approach of surveillance and rapid response running from May through November. When a suspected case is identified, health services trigger: Entomological Investigations: Assessing the local mosquito population. Localized Control: Applying insecticide treatments around the residence of the infected individual. Breeding Site Removal: Intensified efforts to clear standing water. France continues to lead European surveillance in detecting local transmission, though the persistence of the tiger mosquito remains a systemic challenge for temperate regions. analysis.brief_en: France has issued a 2026 chikungunya alert for its southern regions, emphasizing the heightened risk of local transmission due to the tiger mosquito (Aedes albopictus) being established in residential areas. The alert, active from May to November, targets the Mediterranean Corridor, including Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur, Occitanie, and coastal regions. Public health agencies have raised the alert level based on surveillance data, noting that while case numbers are currently below the 2025 peak, the mosquito vector's presence in urban and rural zones suggests potential widespread exposure. The response strategy includes entomological investigations, localized insecticide treatments, and intensified efforts to remove breeding sites. France remains the only European nation reporting locally acquired chikungunya cases in 2026, highlighting the need for vigilance and preventive measures such as repellents, protective clothing, and eliminating standing water. Travelers to these areas are advised to integrate mosquito protection into their travel planning.
