news.content: Skip to content Home The Network Contact Subscribe Home The Network Contact Subscribe News France issues 2026 chikungunya alert for southern regions A record wave of locally acquired chikungunya in 2025 is reshaping 2026 travel advice for southern France, with health agencies urging heightened mosquito protection. Jolyon Zivkov · Aug 26, 2026 The Traveler contains affiliate links. If you click through and make a purchase, we may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you. We are grateful if you use these as it helps a lot! Read the full policy. Table of contents Record local transmission reshapes 2026 risk landscape Southern regions at the center of 2026 travel warnings What the chikungunya alert means for travelers Climate, vector expansion and evolving public health responses How travelers can monitor the situation through 2026 More news on this day Air France restores Dubai and Riyadh flights after six-month halt AAA warns drivers as back‐to‐school traffic risks rise Why Airlines Are Putting Seatback Screens Back in Every Seat France is entering the 2026 mosquito season under an unusual chikungunya alert, after a record number of locally acquired cases in 2025 across southern regions prompted renewed travel cautions and intensified surveillance efforts. Get the latest news straight to your inbox! Record local transmission reshapes 2026 risk landscape Publicly available surveillance data show that mainland France recorded an unprecedented level of local chikungunya transmission in 2025, transforming what had long been considered a mainly imported infection into a growing domestic concern. National surveillance coordinated by Santé publique France documented hundreds of autochthonous cases clustered in dozens of communes, a sharp increase compared with previous years when only sporadic local events were identified. Reports indicate that the bulk of locally acquired infections in 2025 occurred in regions already known for the presence of the invasive tiger mosquito Aedes albopictus, including Provence Alpes Côte d’Azur, Occitanie, Auvergne Rhône Alpes and Corsica. Additional clusters were reported for the first time in regions such as Nouvelle Aquitaine and Grand Est, illustrating how the ecological range of the mosquito and associated arboviruses has moved beyond the Mediterranean corridor. Analyses published by European and French public health agencies underline that these 2025 figures represent the highest burden of locally acquired chikungunya documented in mainland France to date. The early start of some transmission events, combined with large multi week clusters in coastal departments, has led experts to frame the 2026 season as a year of heightened vigilance rather than a return to earlier, lower baseline levels. While chikungunya activity typically peaks between late spring and early autumn, seasonal bulletins emphasize that 2025 saw transmission extend through much of the surveillance window from May to November. This extended period of risk is a key driver of the updated messages now being disseminated to residents and travelers planning trips to the south of France in 2026. Southern regions at the center of 2026 travel warnings Travel oriented advisories for 2026 consistently highlight southern France as the main area of concern for chikungunya, mirroring the geographic pattern of the 2025 clusters. Departments in Provence Alpes Côte d’Azur, particularly along the Mediterranean coast in the Var, Alpes Maritimes and Bouches du Rhône, recorded some of the largest groups of locally acquired cases, with individual communes reporting several dozen infections across the summer months. In neighboring Occitanie, localized transmission was also observed in 2025, contributing to a broader band of risk stretching from the Spanish border across Languedoc and into the lower Rhône valley. Surveillance summaries note that these southern regions combine established populations of Aedes albopictus with substantial tourist flows during the warm months, a combination that increases the likelihood that imported infections can seed local outbreaks. Further north and inland, smaller clusters in Auvergne Rhône Alpes and first time detection of autochthonous infections in regions such as Nouvelle Aquitaine demonstrate that chikungunya is no longer confined to a single coastal strip. Nonetheless, current travel messaging still places the greatest emphasis on the Mediterranean departments, where climatic conditions and mosquito densities are considered most favorable for sustained transmission during summer 2026. International monitoring from the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control points out that the chikungunya situation in mainland France is occurring against a backdrop of elevated transmission in parts of the Indian Ocean and other endemic areas, generating high numbers of imported cases. These imported infections are regarded as the ignition point for local transmission in areas where the tiger mosquito is well established. What the chikungunya alert means for travelers The 2026 chikungunya alert for France does not involve broad movement restrictions, but it is prompting a shift in practical advice for domestic and international travelers heading to southern regions. Public health guidance disseminated through national channels urges anyone visiting colonized areas between May and November to treat mosquito avoidance as a central part of their trip planning, similar to long standing recommendations for dengue and Zika. Information pages from French health institutions describe chikungunya as a viral disease transmitted predominately by daytime biting Aedes mosquitoes, with symptoms that commonly include sudden onset fever and intense joint pain, sometimes accompanied by headache, rash or muscle aches. Although many patients recover within days to weeks, joint symptoms can become prolonged in some individuals, and authorities classify older adults, pregnant people and those with underlying health conditions among groups that may face higher risk of complications. Travel related advisories for 2026 emphasize straightforward protection measures: use of long clothing, insect repellents containing active ingredients endorsed by national guidance, and mosquito screens or air conditioned accommodation where available. Recommendations also stress limiting time in areas with high mosquito density at dawn and dusk, removing standing water around holiday rentals or campsites and promptly seeking medical assessment in case of fever within two weeks of a suspected mosquito exposure. Several information campaigns launched in 2025 and carried into 2026 target both residents and visitors in affected departments, encouraging prompt reporting of suspected cases to healthcare providers and rapid local vector control when clusters are identified. Publicly available briefings indicate that the objective is not to discourage travel, but to lower the probability that imported or early local cases evolve into larger outbreaks during the peak tourist months. Climate, vector expansion and evolving public health responses Researchers and public health agencies are increasingly linking the expanding footprint of chikungunya risk in France to the rapid spread of Aedes albopictus combined with environmental change. Entomological maps compiled by surveillance networks show that, as of the mid 2020s, the tiger mosquito is established in the majority of mainland departments, including many that were not colonized a decade ago, with confirmed presence across much of southern and central France. Scientific analyses cited in media and institutional reports describe how milder winters, warmer summers and changing rainfall patterns have extended the viable season for mosquito activity, particularly in low altitude Mediterranean and Atlantic zones. Modeling work on the ecological niche of Aedes albopictus suggests that suitable habitat for the vector is likely to continue spreading northwards in coming years, raising the prospect that locally acquired arboviral infections could become more common in areas that historically saw only imported cases. In response to the record 2025 chikungunya season, French health services have maintained reinforced arbovirus surveillance for 2026, focusing on early detection of imported cases and rapid investigation of fever clusters in colonized communes. Department level bulletins describe close coordination between human health surveillance, local vector control operators and municipal authorities, with contingency plans for intensified mosquito control around confirmed cases during the May to November period. At the European level, ECDC surveillance outputs continue to monitor both travel associated and locally acquired chikungunya cases across the EU and European Economic Area. These datasets inform regional risk assessments and support targeted communication to travelers, particularly those moving between territories experiencing active outbreaks and areas such as southern France where competent mosquito vectors are widespread. How travelers can monitor the situation through 2026 For those planning trips to Provence, the Côte d’Azur, Corsica or other parts of southern France in 2026, publicly accessible surveillance bulletins and government health portals offer the clearest overview of current chikungunya activity. National reports are typically updated throughout the mosquito season, summarizing the number and location of imported and locally acquired cases, and highlighting departments experiencing active clusters. European monitoring platforms complement this picture with information on transmission in popular long haul destinations, particularly the Indian Ocean and Caribbean territories that have historically been the main source of imported chikungunya infections. Travel health resources advise checking both the situation at the intended destination within France and in any countries visited shortly beforehand, especially where onward travel to the Mediterranean coast is planned. Health agencies also encourage travelers returning from chikungunya affected regions outside Europe to remain alert to symptoms after they arrive in France or elsewhere in the EU. Early medical consultation in case of fever and joint pain helps clinicians distinguish chikungunya from dengue, COVID 19 and other febrile illnesses, and facilitates rapid public health investigation in areas where the tiger mosquito is present. Overall, the 2026 chikungunya alert underscores how rapidly vector borne disease patterns can shift in temperate countries with established Aedes populations. For travelers, the key message is that trips to southern France remain feasible, but that robust mosquito protection and attentiveness to official health updates are now an integral part of safe travel planning during the summer and early autumn months. Get the latest news straight to your inbox! Record local transmission reshapes 2026 risk landscape Publicly available surveillance data show that mainland France recorded an unprecedented level of local chikungunya transmission in 2025, transforming what had long been considered a mainly imported infection into a growing domestic concern. National surveillance coordinated by Santé publique France documented hundreds of autochthonous cases clustered in dozens of communes, a sharp increase compared with previous years when only sporadic local events were identified. Reports indicate that the bulk of locally acquired infections in 2025 occurred in regions already known for the presence of the invasive tiger mosquito Aedes albopictus, including Provence Alpes Côte d’Azur, Occitanie, Auvergne Rhône Alpes and Corsica. Additional clusters were reported for the first time in regions such as Nouvelle Aquitaine and Grand Est, illustrating how the ecological range of the mosquito and associated arboviruses has moved beyond the Mediterranean corridor. Analyses published by European and French public health agencies underline that these 2025 figures represent the highest burden of locally acquired chikungunya documented in mainland France to date. The early start of some transmission events, combined with large multi week clusters in coastal departments, has led experts to frame the 2026 season as a year of heightened vigilance rather than a return to earlier, lower baseline levels. While chikungunya activity typically peaks between late spring and early autumn, seasonal bulletins emphasize that 2025 saw transmission extend through much of the surveillance window from May to November. This extended period of risk is a key driver of the updated messages now being disseminated to residents and travelers planning trips to the south of France in 2026. Southern regions at the center of 2026 travel warnings Travel oriented advisories for 2026 consistently highlight southern France as the main area of concern for chikungunya, mirroring the geographic pattern of the 2025 clusters. Departments in Provence Alpes Côte d’Azur, particularly along the Mediterranean coast in the Var, Alpes Maritimes and Bouches du Rhône, recorded some of the largest groups of locally acquired cases, with individual communes reporting several dozen infections across the summer months. In neighboring Occitanie, localized transmission was also observed in 2025, contributing to a broader band of risk stretching from the Spanish border across Languedoc and into the lower Rhône valley. Surveillance summaries note that these southern regions combine established populations of Aedes albopictus with substantial tourist flows during the warm months, a combination that increases the likelihood that imported infections can seed local outbreaks. Further north and inland, smaller clusters in Auvergne Rhône Alpes and first time detection of autochthonous infections in regions such as Nouvelle Aquitaine demonstrate that chikungunya is no longer confined to a single coastal strip. Nonetheless, current travel messaging still places the greatest emphasis on the Mediterranean departments, where climatic conditions and mosquito densities are considered most favorable for sustained transmission during summer 2026. International monitoring from the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control points out that the chikungunya situation in mainland France is occurring against a backdrop of elevated transmission in parts of the Indian Ocean and other endemic areas, generating high numbers of imported cases. These imported infections are regarded as the ignition point for local transmission in areas where the tiger mosquito is well established. What the chikungunya alert means for travelers The 2026 chikungunya alert for France does not involve broad movement restrictions, but it is prompting a shift in practical advice for domestic and international travelers heading to southern regions. Public health guidance disseminated through national channels urges anyone visiting colonized areas between May and November to treat mosquito avoidance as a central part of their trip planning, similar to long standing recommendations for dengue and Zika. Information pages from French health institutions describe chikungunya as a viral disease transmitted predominately by daytime biting Aedes mosquitoes, with symptoms that commonly include sudden onset fever and intense joint pain, sometimes accompanied by headache, rash or muscle aches. Although many patients recover within days to weeks, joint symptoms can become prolonged in some individuals, and authorities classify older adults, pregnant people and those with underlying health conditions among groups that may face higher risk of complications. Travel related advisories for 2026 emphasize straightforward protection measures: use of long clothing, insect repellents containing active ingredients endorsed by national guidance, and mosquito screens or air conditioned accommodation where available. Recommendations also stress limiting time in areas with high mosquito density at dawn and dusk, removing standing water around holiday rentals or campsites and promptly seeking medical assessment in case of fever within two weeks of a suspected mosquito exposure. Several information campaigns launched in 2025 and carried into 2026 target both residents and visitors in affected departments, encouraging prompt reporting of suspected cases to healthcare providers and rapid local vector control when clusters are identified. Publicly available briefings indicate that the objective is not to discourage travel, but to lower the probability that imported or early local cases evolve into larger outbreaks during the peak tourist months. Climate, vector expansion and evolving public health responses Researchers and public health agencies are increasingly linking the expanding footprint of chikungunya risk in France to the rapid spread of Aedes albopictus combined with environmental change. Entomological maps compiled by surveillance networks show that, as of the mid 2020s, the tiger mosquito is established in the majority of mainland departments, including many that were not colonized a decade ago, with confirmed presence across much of southern and central France. Scientific analyses cited in media and institutional reports describe how milder winters, warmer summers and changing rainfall patterns have extended the viable season for mosquito activity, particularly in low altitude Mediterranean and Atlantic zones. Modeling work on the ecological niche of Aedes albopictus suggests that suitable habitat for the vector is likely to continue spreading northwards in coming years, raising the prospect that locally acquired arboviral infections could become more common in areas that historically saw only imported cases. In response to the record 2025 chikungunya season, French health services have maintained reinforced arbovirus surveillance for 2026, focusing on early detection of imported cases and rapid investigation of fever clusters in colonized communes. Department level bulletins describe close coordination between human health surveillance, local vector control operators and municipal authorities, with contingency plans for intensified mosquito control around confirmed cases during the May to November period. At the European level, ECDC surveillance outputs continue to monitor both travel associated and locally acquired chikungunya cases across the EU and European Economic Area. These datasets inform regional risk assessments and support targeted communication to travelers, particularly those moving between territories experiencing active outbreaks and areas such as southern France where competent mosquito vectors are widespread. How travelers can monitor the situation through 2026 For those planning trips to Provence, the Côte d’Azur, Corsica or other parts of southern France in 2026, publicly accessible surveillance bulletins and government health portals offer the clearest overview of current chikungunya activity. National reports are typically updated throughout the mosquito season, summarizing the number and location of imported and locally acquired cases, and highlighting departments experiencing active clusters. European monitoring platforms complement this picture with information on transmission in popular long haul destinations, particularly the Indian Ocean and Caribbean territories that have historically been the main source of imported chikungunya infections. Travel health resources advise checking both the situation at the intended destination within France and in any countries visited shortly beforehand, especially where onward travel to the Mediterranean coast is planned. Health agencies also encourage travelers returning from chikungunya affected regions outside Europe to remain alert to symptoms after they arrive in France or elsewhere in the EU. Early medical consultation in case of fever and joint pain helps clinicians distinguish chikungunya from dengue, COVID 19 and other febrile illnesses, and facilitates rapid public health investigation in areas where the tiger mosquito is present. Overall, the 2026 chikungunya alert underscores how rapidly vector borne disease patterns can shift in temperate countries with established Aedes populations. For travelers, the key message is that trips to southern France remain feasible, but that robust mosquito protection and attentiveness to official health updates are now an integral part of safe travel planning during the summer and early autumn months. elements_zh.event: 由于 2025 年本地感染病例数量创历史新高,法国发布了 2026 年基孔肯雅热警报,这促使人们重新发出旅行警告并加强了 监测 工作。该警报基于法国 Santé publique 协调的国家 监测 的确认数据。

news.content_title: Typhoid cases rise slightly in Telangana as dengue, malaria and chikungunya decline
news.content: Typhoid cases have shown a slight increase in Telangana this year even as cases of dengue, malaria, chikungunya, acute diarrhoeal disease and dysentery have declined compared with the corresponding period last year, according to a note released by the Telangana Health Minister’s office on Saturday (August 29). The figures were discussed during a review meeting chaired by Health Minister C. Damodar Raja Narasimha, where officials assessed the seasonal disease situation amid the ongoing monsoon, district-wise trends, fever surveys, mosquito-control measures and the preparedness of government hospitals. According to the note, a comparison of cases recorded between January 1 and August 27 this year with the corresponding period last year showed a decline in dengue, malaria, chikungunya, acute diarrhoeal disease and dysentery cases. Typhoid cases registered a slight increase. Officials said special attention was being given to areas where disease cases were showing an upward trend. The Minister instructed health officials to visit districts reporting increases in cases, assess the situation on the ground and take necessary preventive measures. He also directed all government hospitals to remain fully prepared to deal with seasonal diseases and emergencies. The Minister also called for heightened vigilance against Influenza-Like Illness (ILI) in Telangana in view of rising seasonal influenza and swine flu cases reported in Delhi and Maharashtra. He directed officials to monitor ILI cases reported daily by both government and private hospitals and submit a weekly report to the government. Officials informed the Minister that reagents required for all necessary tests were available and that the seasonal influenza situation in Telangana was currently under control, the note said. The Minister called for special focus on villages, towns, schools, hostels, construction sites and other high-risk locations. ASHA workers and ANMs were directed to conduct door-to-door visits and create awareness among residents about preventing seasonal diseases and mosquito breeding. Hospital Child Deaths PMC standing committee orders daily anti-mosquito drives amid dengue & chikungunya fears, seeks quick deployment of 265 employees Sarang Dastane / Aug 28, 2026, 00:55 IST Comments Share AA +Text Size Small Medium Large STING ALERT Pune: PMC standing committee on Thursday directed the civic health department and all 15 ward offices to conduct daily spraying and fogging drives at vulnerable locations amid fears of a rise in dengue and chikungunya cases.Standing committee chairperson Shrinath Bhimale also instructed health inspectors to visit housing societies and open plots to ensure that stagnant water, a key mosquito-breeding source, was promptly eliminated. He further told Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) to expedite the appointment of 265 workers on contract to strengthen mosquito-control measures across the city.The directive comes as several corporators demanded intensified fogging and spraying drives, citing a growing number of complaints from residents about fever and other health-related issues. Mahesh Pokale, an activist from the Sinhagad Road area who recently submitted a representation to the local ward office, said PMC must go beyond spraying activities and launch awareness campaigns. “Citizens should be encouraged to seek immediate medical attention if they develop symptoms of dengue or chikungunya,” he said.Corporator Vaishali Banakar from Hadapsar flagged irregularities in spraying operations and urged PMC to prioritise repairs of damaged drainage lines. by Taboolaby Taboola Sponsored LinksSponsored Links Promoted LinksPromoted Links You May Like Squirt Some Honey on Your Dog's Tongue, Here's What HappensDog's Daily Health Undo “Contaminated drain water mixing with potable water is a serious concern. PMC must address this issue on priority,” she said, adding that continuous rainfall and fluctuating temperatures in Aug contributed to a spike in cases.PMC officials said they already filled 150 permanent posts dedicated to mosquito-control work. The proposal to recruit an additional 265 contractual employees, however, remains pending. Bhimale said he has sought an explanation from officials for the delay.According to PMC data, the civic body has issued 1,708 notices and collected Rs 2.65 lakh in fine this year after detecting mosquito-breeding sites. drives at vulnerable locations amid fears of a rise in dengue and chikungunya cases.Standing committee chairperson Shrinath Bhimale also instructed health inspectors to visit housing societies and open plots to ensure that stagnant water, a key mosquito-breeding source, was promptly eliminated. He further told Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) to expedite the appointment of 265 workers on contract to strengthen mosquito-control measures across the city.The directive comes as several corporators demanded intensified fogging and spraying drives, citing a growing number of complaints from residents about fever and other health-related issues. Mahesh Pokale, an activist from the Sinhagad Road area who recently submitted a representation to the local ward office, said PMC must go beyond spraying activities and launch awareness campaigns. “Citizens should be encouraged to seek immediate medical attention if they develop symptoms of dengue or chikungunya,” he said.Corporator Vaishali Banakar from Hadapsar flagged irregularities in spraying operations and urged PMC to prioritise repairs of damaged drainage lines. by Taboolaby Taboola Sponsored LinksSponsored Links Promoted LinksPromoted Links You May Like Squirt Some Honey on Your Dog's Tongue, Here's What HappensDog's Daily Health Undo “Contaminated drain water mixing with potable water is a serious concern. PMC must address this issue on priority,” she said, adding that continuous rainfall and fluctuating temperatures in Aug contributed to a spike in cases.PMC officials said they already filled 150 permanent posts dedicated to mosquito-control work. The proposal to recruit an additional 265 contractual employees, however, remains pending. Bhimale said he has sought an explanation from officials for the delay.According to PMC data, the civic body has issued 1,708 notices and collected Rs 2.65 lakh in fine this year after detecting mosquito-breeding sites. news.content_zh: 为了应对登革热和基孔肯雅热病例可能增加的担忧,浦那市政府 (PMC) 常务委员会于 2026 年 8 月 27 日下令每天进行灭蚊喷洒和雾化活动。该指令的发布是为了解决对积水(蚊子的主要繁殖源)日益增长的担忧,并消除与这些疾病相关的健康风险。卫生检查员奉命走访住房协会和空地,以确保及时解决积水问题。该委员会还以喷洒作业不规范以及8月份持续降雨和气温波动的影响为由,寻求加快任命265名合同工,以加强灭蚊工作。PMC 官员表示,150 个长期职位已经填补,但增聘工人的提议仍有待确定。该行动是缓解基孔肯雅热和登革热传播的持续应对措施的一部分,目的是保护浦那的公众健康。
